topStory.headline: Community College Students Selected for New Jersey A.I. Fellowship
topStory.summary:
Two Middlesex College computer science students, Laila Diaz and Hassan Ibrahim, have been selected from over 250 applicants for New Jersey's A.I. for Impact Community College Fellowship. The semester-long program pairs students with the state's Office of Innovation, where they work 20 hours per week on government A.I. projects while receiving stipends and continuing their studies.

Ibrahim is developing machine learning models to streamline I.T. ticketing systems for state government operations. Diaz is creating an A.I. Slack bot to help engineers search data and find source citations. Both projects address operational challenges in government settings.

Ibrahim stated his interest in working with A.I. "in an ethical way" and understanding "how A.I. systems work in a regulated, government setting." Diaz expressed interest in cybersecurity work for government, describing it as "working for my community."

The New Jersey Council of County Colleges administers the program, with funding from the Economic Development Authority. The fellowship model connects community college students directly to career pathways in government technology roles while providing practical experience with A.I. implementation in institutional settings.

stories.headline: Stanford Study Questions A.I. Classroom Tool Effectiveness
stories.summary: Stanford researchers have found limited evidence that A.I. tools improve student learning long-term. According to GovTech, while students perform better while using A.I. tools, those gains often disappear when the tools are removed. The research raises concerns about cognitive offloading, where students may become dependent on A.I. assistance rather than developing underlying skills. The findings suggest A.I. tools may help with immediate task completion but may not contribute to lasting skill development.

stories.headline: University of Houston Adopts Google A.I. Education Suite
stories.summary: The University of Houston has partnered with Google to provide campus-wide access to Gemini for Education and NotebookLM. According to The Daily Cougar, the university is emphasizing preparing students to be "A.I.-fluent" as part of the initiative. Faculty are being urged to set clear guidelines for ethical A.I. use in coursework. The partnership gives students and faculty access to Google's educational A.I. tools across the university.

stories.headline: Babson Writing Professor Integrates A.I. Into Classroom Practice
stories.summary: A writing professor at Babson College has shared her experience integrating A.I. into educational settings. According to The North Star Monthly, the professor's approach evolved from initial A.I. experimentation to a more structured method balancing tool use with critical thinking development. The focus centers on helping students develop discernment about when A.I. supports learning versus when it substitutes for learning.
